subject: general
question: Who was the President of the Constituent Assembly of India after independence?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. Rajendra Prasad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. Rajendra Prasad **was the **first president of India**, serving from 1950 to 1962.
 
• He was a lawyer, scholar, and politician. He became a significant leader in the Bihar and Maharashtra regions of the Indian National Congress during the Indian Independence Movement.
 
• During the Salt Satyagraha of 1930 and the Quit India campaign of 1942, British authorities imprisoned Prasad, a devotee of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• Prasad became **Minister of Food and Agriculture** in the federal government after the constituent assembly elections in 1946.
 
• Prasad was chosen as **President of the Constituent Assembly of India**, which drafted the Indian Constitution and served as the country's provisional Parliament when the country gained independence in 1947.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Constituent Assembly of India**, which was constituted by representatives of provincial assemblies elected by the Indian people, drafted the Constitution. President of the Constituent Assembly for the first time was** Dr. Sachidanand Sinha.**
 
• **Dr. Rajendra Prasad** was later chosen president of the organization.
 
• Dr. BR Ambedkar, the chairman of the Constitution's Drafting Committee, is widely regarded as the chief architect of the Indian Constitution, which provides a comprehensive and dynamic framework for guiding and governing the country while taking into account the country's unique social, cultural, and religious diversity.
 
• **Chakravarti Rajagopalachari**, popularly known as Rajaji or C.R., also known as Mootharignar Rajaji, was an Indian statesman, writer, lawyer, and independence activist. Rajagopalachari was the** last Governor-General of India**, as India became a republic in 1950.
 
• **Acharya Narendra Dev** was one of the leading theorists of the Congress Socialist Party in India. His democratic socialism renounced violent means as a matter of principle and embraced the satyagraha as a revolutionary tactic.
